concepts.def: Plant diseases can be detected from observable signs on the plant: stunted growth, spots on leaves, areas of decay (rot), growths, malformed stems or leaves, discolouration, and the presence of pests.

Once a disease has been detected, it can be identified by reference to a gardening manual or website, by taking infected plants to a laboratory to identify the pathogen, or by using testing kits that contain monoclonal antibodies.

A viral pathogen of plants. It gives a distinctive mosaic pattern of discolouration on the leaves; because the discoloured areas contain less chlorophyll, less photosynthesis occurs and the growth of the plant is affected.
A fungal disease of roses. Purple or black spots develop on the leaves, which often turn yellow and drop early, so less photosynthesis occurs and the growth of the plant is affected.
Insects that infest plants and feed on them, taking dissolved sugars and other nutrients from the plant and so weakening it. Aphids are insects, not pathogens.
Nitrate ions are needed by a plant for protein synthesis and therefore for growth. A plant grown in soil short of nitrate ions shows stunted growth.
Magnesium ions are needed by a plant to make chlorophyll. A plant short of magnesium ions cannot make enough chlorophyll and shows chlorosis, in which the leaves turn yellow.
Structures that resist invasion of microorganisms: cellulose cell walls, a tough waxy cuticle on leaves, and layers of dead cells around stems (bark on trees) which fall off.
Substances a plant produces to defend itself: antibacterial chemicals, and poisons to deter herbivores.
Adaptations that protect a plant from animals: thorns and hairs which deter animals, leaves which droop or curl when touched, and mimicry to trick animals.

mcqs.q: A plant has grown to the normal height for its age, but its leaves have turned yellow. What is the most likely cause?
options: A lack of nitrate ions, needed to make chlorophyll
A lack of magnesium ions, needed to make chlorophyll
An infection by black spot, a fungal plant disease
An attack by aphids, which are plant microorganisms
mcqs.explain: Magnesium ions are needed to make chlorophyll, so a magnesium deficiency causes chlorosis, in which the leaves turn yellow while height can stay normal.

mcqs.q: Which of these plant problems is caused by a fungal pathogen?
options: Black spot, giving dark marks on rose leaves
Aphid infestation, giving reduced plant growth
Chlorosis, giving yellow patches on leaves
Tobacco mosaic virus, giving a mosaic pattern
mcqs.explain: Black spot is the named fungal disease of plants: purple or black spots develop on the leaves, which often turn yellow and drop early.

mcqs.q: A rose plant has sharp thorns on its stems. Which type of plant defence is this?
options: A physical defence that resists microorganisms
A chemical defence that kills invading bacteria
A sign of infection by a fungal plant pathogen
A mechanical adaptation that deters animals
mcqs.explain: Thorns and hairs deter animals, so they are listed as mechanical adaptations rather than as physical or chemical defence responses.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a physical defence response that resists invasion of microorganisms?
options: Poisons which are made in the leaves
Hairs which grow on the leaf surfaces
Leaves which curl when they are touched
Layers of dead cells around the stems
mcqs.explain: Layers of dead cells around stems (bark on trees), which fall off, are a physical defence response that resists invasion of microorganisms.

mcqs.q: A grower sees stunted growth and discoloured leaves on a crop, and a gardening website does not settle what is wrong. What should be done next to identify the cause?
options: Add nitrate fertiliser to the soil to restore leaf colour
Spray the whole crop with a fungicide to kill black spot
Take the plant to a laboratory to identify the pathogen
Look for a mosaic pattern to confirm a fungal disease
mcqs.explain: Identification can be made by taking infected plants to a laboratory to identify the pathogen, which is the step to take when a gardening manual or website is not enough.
